decisions.reason: As a newly launched flagship closely aligned with the firm's strategic push in reusable packaging, it is an option the firm is very likely to keep open because uncertainty is still high and early withdrawal would be premature.

A foldable large container line with several models and its own page suggests meaningful commitment in a core category, so management would likely continue learning from the market rather than abandon it after only one year.

Although it had lower website prominence, a stackable plastic crate line fits the firm's established capabilities and customer base, making it inexpensive enough to keep while demand information accumulates.

The medium-duty rackable pallet line is relevant to the core transport-packaging business, and with little time for results to fully resolve its value, the firm would usually retain it as a live option.
Its own page and niche usefulness in spill-retention indicate a deliberate market test in an adjacent application, so a large firm would likely keep it available unless clear failure emerged.

This pallet variant is somewhat narrower than the broader product lines, but because it still leverages existing pallet capabilities and launch costs are likely recoverable only over time, management would more likely keep than drop it.
